questions.prompt: Which of the following functions is differentiable at $x=0$?
questions.explanation: $x|x|$ equals $x^{2}$ for $x\geq 0$ and $-x^{2}$ for $x<0$. Both one-sided derivatives at $0$ are $0$, so it is differentiable at $0$. The others have a corner or cusp at $0$.

questions.explanation:
Differentiate: $3x^{2}+3y^{2}y'-3(y+xy')=0$, so

$$
y'=\dfrac{y-x^{2}}{y^{2}-x}.
$$

At $\left(\dfrac{3}{2},\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ this equals $-1$.

questions.prompt: The maximum value of $f(x)=x e^{-x}$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=e^{-x}(1-x)=0$ at $x=1$. Since $f''(1)=-\dfrac{1}{e}<0$, $f(1)=\dfrac{1}{e}$ is the global maximum.

questions.prompt: The height of the right circular cylinder of maximum volume that can be inscribed in a sphere of radius $5$ is
questions.explanation: For a sphere of radius $5$, $r^{2}=25-\dfrac{h^{2}}{4}$. Then $V=\pi h\left(25-\dfrac{h^{2}}{4}\right)$ and $V'(h)=\pi\left(25-\dfrac{3h^{2}}{4}\right)=0$ gives $h=\dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{3}$.

questions.prompt: The points on the curve $y=x^{2}$ closest to the point $(0, 2)$ are
questions.explanation: Minimize $d^{2}=x^{2}+(x^{2}-2)^{2}$. Setting the derivative to zero gives $x=0$ or $x=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$. At $x=0$, $d=2$; at $x=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$, $d^{2}=\dfrac{7}{4}$. So the closest points are $\left(\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}},\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$.

questions.prompt: For $f(x)=x^{2}$ on $[1, 3]$, the value of $c$ guaranteed by the Mean Value Theorem is
A $13\,\mathrm{m}$ ladder leans against a wall. The bottom is $5\,\mathrm{m}$ from the wall and is sliding away at $2\,\mathrm{m/s}$. The top is sliding down at the rate
questions.explanation:
$x^{2}+y^{2}=13^{2}=169$. With $x=5$, $y=12$. Differentiating gives $2x\dfrac{dx}{dt}+2y\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$, so

$$
\left|\dfrac{dy}{dt}\right|=\dfrac{x}{y}\cdot\left|\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right|=\dfrac{5}{6}.
$$

The top slides down at $\dfrac{5}{6}\,\mathrm{m/s}$.

questions.prompt: If $f(x)=3\sin x+4\cos x-kx$ is decreasing for every real $x$, then
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=3\cos x-4\sin x-k$. The expression $3\cos x-4\sin x$ has amplitude $5$, so $f'(x)\leq 0$ for all $x$ iff $k\geq 5$.
